transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date: 2026-04-16 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Carlos (Redwood), Dr. Priya Nair (CISO Aurora), Marcus Lee (Head of Cloud), Denise O'Connor (Security PM), Samir Patel (Legal)

Summary (auto): Quick posture review; focus on KMS/BYOK and trust center access. Agreement to share redacted reports and schedule deeper technical POC.

[00:00] Sophie Martinez: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — I think we've got like 40 minutes, so we'll try to run through our posture docs and answer questions. Hey Priya, Marcus, Denise, Samir.
[00:12] Dr. Priya Nair: Hi Sophie, thanks. We just wanted to make sure the high level first — what artifacts we'll get and how we can map controls to our internal GRC.
[00:20] Sophie Martinez: Totally. Liam will run the technical parts — I'll cover the Trust Center and the reports we can share.
[00:28] Liam Chen: Hey all. Quick note, I'll talk about KMS options, BYOK, and audit logs — and we can dig into the Private deployment path if you want.
[00:36] Marcus Lee: Great. Our top concerns are: audit log retention for PHI flows, key management (we prefer BYOK/HSM) and ensuring RBAC for trust center doesn't give too much blast radius to engineers.
[00:50] Denise O'Connor: Also evidence collection cadence — auditors want a timeline.
[01:03] Sophie Martinez: Understood. On artifacts, we can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report, an ISO 27001 attestation summary, and a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps our controls to typical frameworks. We'll drop those in Trust Center and give you read-only access.
[01:20] Dr. Priya Nair: When you say "Trust Center" — is that a self-service portal where we can pull logs/evidence or just a repo for reports?
[01:29] Sophie Martinez: It's a portal. You get doc downloads, policy artifacts, and an evidence request flow. You can also link in to download audit log exports. Access is RBAC'd — we set org roles and you can create reviewer accounts.
[01:42] Marcus Lee: Are reviewer accounts SSO-enabled? We use Okta with SCIM.
[01:48] Liam Chen: Yes, SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning are supported. There's a couple of pre-built roles — org-admin, compliance-reviewer, and viewer. You can customize roles if you need more granularity.
[02:00] Samir Patel: On data residency: we have patients in EU and US. For EU clinical workloads we need logs and storage to stay in EU. How does Redwood support region scoping?
[02:12] Liam Chen: We have region routing policies. For hosted customers you can pick region-locations and we can pin inference to EU regions. For Dedicated or Private deployments you can run entirely VPC/EU-only. Note: exporting aggregated logs across regions is possible but raw PHI should remain in-region if you choose that option.
[02:30] Denise O'Connor: Any documented SLA or attestation that data won't cross region boundaries?
[02:35] Sophie Martinez: Yes, in the Trust Center we'll share our data residency configuration docs and the controls map showing the measures we take. For Dedicated/Private we also provide contractual language around data locality.
[02:48] Dr. Priya Nair: KMS — we require customer-controlled keys for encryption at rest. Do you support BYOK or HSM integrations?
[02:56] Liam Chen: We support multiple KMS models: managed Redwood KMS, cloud-provider KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault), and BYOK where you hold the root key in your KMS and we perform envelope encryption. For Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your HSM via VPN/VPC peering and customer-managed key policies.
[03:16] Marcus Lee: How about key rotation and auditability?
[03:20] Liam Chen: Rotation is supported — we log key operations and expose key-use logs for audit. We can also show evidence of separation of duties for key admin roles in the control map.
[03:30] Sophie Martinez: Small note on terminology — sometimes our transcripts call "KV cache" weird, you'll see K-V cash in older docs, ignore that.
[03:38] Dr. Priya Nair: Haha we noticed earlier in a deck.
[03:42] Liam Chen: On audit logs: we keep system and admin audit logs for 365 days by default, with extended retention options. You can export logs in JSON lines or push to your SIEM with a secure forwarder. If you need longer retention for compliance, we can add an archival pipeline to S3 in-region and set retention per your policy.
[04:05] Denise O'Connor: For SOC 2 evidence, how does evidence collection work for things like change control tickets or config snapshots?
[04:12] Sophie Martinez: There's an evidence request workflow in Trust Center. We can attach config snapshots, ticket links, and signed attestation letters. We try to provide everything auditors generally ask for — and we use a controls matrix so you can map our control IDs to your control IDs.
[04:29] Marcus Lee: What about encryption of logs themselves? Are those encrypted at rest and in transit?
[04:35] Liam Chen: Yes, logs are encrypted both in transit (TLS) and at rest (envelope encryption). If you use your KMS keys, logs that contain PHI can be encrypted under your customer-managed key.
[04:46] Samir Patel: Any redaction preprocessing you do in logs to remove PHI before sending to our SIEM?
[04:52] Liam Chen: We don't do automatic redaction of raw application logs by default; we can configure a pipeline to mask or filter fields before export as part of a POC. We'll want to design that with your team because it's easy to accidentally remove fields auditors expect.
[05:10] Dr. Priya Nair: Control mapping — can you give an example of how your control maps to ISO 27001 Annex A?
[05:17] Sophie Martinez: Sure — our access control policy links to A.9 controls; we provide the policy, evidence of user access reviews, and the RBAC implementation details. In the controls spreadsheet you'll see rows like "RW-AC-1" mapped to ISO A.9.2 and SOC 2 CC6.
[05:34] Denise O'Connor: How are incidents and breach notifications handled? Our auditors want proof of an incident response plan and a few anonymized incident reports.
[05:43] Liam Chen: We have an incident response policy and post-mortems. We can share redacted incident reports and the incident timeline examples in Trust Center. Notifications follow our contractual timelines and we can include notification SLAs in the contract.
[05:56] Marcus Lee: Is there any personnel PII in the reports we get from Trust Center? We need to avoid HR data crossing.
[06:02] Sophie Martinez: We redact personal data from reports where appropriate; the redacted SOC 2 will have names removed and replaced with roles when necessary.
[06:12] Dr. Priya Nair: On RBAC, we need to restrict the ability to create API keys and rotate them. Can you scope roles so only certain people can do key rotations and developers can't?
[06:22] Liam Chen: Yes — roles are granular. You can split responsibilities: key admin, deployment admin, logs viewer, billing viewer. Key rotations can be limited to the key-admin role.
[06:33] Samir Patel: Legal note — we might ask for a sub-process in the contract to verify that RBAC controls are active every quarter. Is that something Redwood would accept?
[06:41] Sophie Martinez: We can include audit checkpoints and provide evidence quarterly. We'll need to pass that to legal and our CS team to agree on contract language.
[06:51] Denise O'Connor: Can you walk briefly through a Private deployment option and what evidence looks like there?
[06:58] Liam Chen: Private deployment is where you run the control plane in your VPC or an on-prem appliance and we provide a customer-managed runtime. Evidence in that case includes architecture diagrams, network ACLs, patched runtime versions, and KMS integration attestations. You'd also get full control over where logs are stored.
[07:20] Marcus Lee: For a POC of Private, what's the rough timeline and what we should expect?
[07:25] Liam Chen: Typical POC is 4-6 weeks: 1 week scoping, 1-2 weeks deployment and integration (KMS, VPC peering), then 1-2 weeks validation with your auditors and our security. We'll provide a checklist.
[07:38] Dr. Priya Nair: That sounds reasonable. What about cost for Dedicated vs Private? We need ballpark for budgeting.
[07:45] Sophie Martinez: We'll send a pricing note — Dedicated is committed capacity with monthly contract, Private has a platform fee plus integration support. I'll include pricing for POC options in the follow-up.
[07:55] Denise O'Connor: For SOC 2 Type II, will the auditor comments be included or just the attestation?
[08:01] Sophie Martinez: The redacted report includes the description of tests and the opinion. Detailed auditor workpapers are not shared but we can provide the control descriptions and evidence that map to the tests.
[08:12] Marcus Lee: Any known major open findings in last period?
[08:15] Liam Chen: No open high findings. There were a few low/medium items around internal docs that were addressed; we'll note them in the control map.
[08:25] Samir Patel: Competitors question — is there anything feature-wise Redwood does differently from BigCloudAI?
[08:31] Sophie Martinez: Our focus is the inference runtime + production observability plus a standardized Trust Center and policy-first controls mapping. Some competitors have docs but not the same integrated evidence workflows and private deployment patterns.
[08:44] Dr. Priya Nair: Ok, next steps?
[08:47] Sophie Martinez: We'll share the redacted SOC 2 and control map within two business days, Liam will provision Trust Center read-only access, Marcus to confirm residency scope, Denise to share reviewer list. We'll compile action items and send meeting notes.
[09:00] Marcus Lee: Sounds good.
[09:03] Denise O'Connor: Quick question — can we get sample API logs so our SIEM team can test ingestion?
[09:09] Liam Chen: Yes, we'll produce sample JSON lines and a sample forwarding config for your SIEM. I'll attach that to the Trust Center folder.
[09:18] Sophie Martinez: Great. Any final legal asks?
[09:20] Samir Patel: Not yet. We'll review redacted report and come back with contract questions.
[09:24] Sophie Martinez: Perfect. We'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the technical deep-dive for the week of 2026-04-27. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript. Notes: transcription has some small errors (speaker overlap and occasional mis-heard acronyms), confirmed medium quality.
